cases.title: Pinned ShadowCode is installed, launches in the live session and survives an open/close soak
Real code, cited document and media missions complete with validated artifacts
cases.notes: WAIVED (code sub-part only; the release owner's 5.0.0 limit). PROVEN on the installed 5.0.1 engine and the production worker service, in the VM upgraded from the shipped 5.0.0 install against this repository: mission_acceptance.py 15/15 (the 5.0.0 harness, unchanged). (a) MEDIA: offline-media mission (real ffmpeg, network none) to review; receipt artifact sizes and SHA-256 re-verified; output independently probed as 48 kHz PCM WAV and fully decoded; source untouched; accepted. (b) CITED DOCUMENT: localmodel sourced_report with real inference through a labelled QA relay exposing one user-supplied local model (Qwen3-4B-Instruct Q6_K, no account) at the provider socket (2 chat calls); citations re-validated in range, source register hashes equal the files, sources untouched, sandbox network none, no credentials, sole read grant the socket directory; accepted. Plus the 5.0.1 Mission Control fixes on the installed engine: same-second missions ran in creation order (order-5.0.1.json), a queued mission reports its review-gate hold in show, list and Mission Control (hold-5.0.1.json, upgrade-final/gui), the busy-database probe, and the 25 regression tests OK (2 skipped: no strace in the guest); make test missions suite 1,112 OK. NOT PROVEN: (c) CODE: the localmodel code mission ran a real turn, left calc.py unchanged and failed on the real unit test (observations.code_localmodel); Codex and Claude were not exercised (paid account).

waiver.reason: 5.0.1 re-ran MISSION-01 on its own installed engine: the media and cited-report missions passed 15/15 against these packages. Only the code mission is unproven, for the reason the release owner accepted for 5.0.0 and that still holds: no keyless provider can edit a workspace (localmodel is chat-only, and its observed code mission failed its test), and Codex or Claude need a paid account that release QA does not use.

cases.title: Cancellation, retry, interrupted service recovery and no duplicated side effects
cases.notes: Against the INSTALLED 5.0.1 engine (shadowfetch-missions 5.0.1-1) and the production user worker service, in the VM upgraded from the shipped 5.0.0 install for UPGRADE-01 (same repository, Packages fd0b98c2...). (1) durable_worker_acceptance.py 9/9: production unit kernel limits (pids.max 128, memory.max 4 GiB, cpu.max 200%); a private real worker SIGKILLed inside checkpoint preparation is recorded failed, never replayed, source byte-identical, no output; a required-checkpoint storage failure refuses execution with a failed receipt; per-scope firebreak limits. (2) durable_service.py 15/15: the production shadowfetch-missions.service SIGKILLed during a real sandboxed media export, systemd restart, the interrupted mission failed and not replayed, the sandboxed process did not outlive it to publish output, an explicit retry ran exactly once more and published exactly one result, undo restored. (3) Cancellation under load: the busy-database probe on 5.0.1 saved and answered Stop in 2.1 s inside the lock wait, show/list answered while a write lock was held, and the worker recorded the saved Stop exactly once; the same probe on the 5.0.0 engine failed (Stop 10.1 s, lost). (4) The 25 5.0.1 mission regression tests on the installed engine: OK (23 ran, 2 strace-dependent skipped in the guest); against the 5.0.0 engine 8 failures and 14 errors. (5) make test: the missions suite (1,112 tests, OK, 6 skipped) including test_cancellation, test_worker_loop, test_worker_wakeup, test_provenance_and_interruption, test_review_lock, test_state_machine, test_audit_chain and the four 5.0.1 regression modules. The harness scripts are the 5.0.0 ones, unchanged (copies in upgrade-final/driver/, not recorded here because they are 5.0.0 evidence); every result here is a new run.

candidate_note: APT-only update (tools/release/versions/5.0.1.toml: delivery = "apt-only", base_release = "5.0.0"). No 5.0.1 image is built: iso_path, iso_sha256, iso_size_bytes and signature_path name the BASE image, 5.0.0's ISO 2d8a72e0 (4085778432 bytes), copied exactly from qa/5.0.0/acceptance.json; UPGRADE-01 starts from an install of it. apt_packages_sha256 and apt_sources_sha256 are the digests of repo/dists/umbra/main/binary-amd64/Packages and main/source/Sources from the final umask-022 build of release/5.0.1 in the authorized publishing tree (sources unchanged since 3ef3ef8; it carries the shadowfetch-fireproof self-upgrade and no-removals fixes and ShadowCode 1.0.1; Valid-Until 2027-03-30). They replace 9953f138/ccea3f0d: packages/ is unchanged since that build, but archive members carry this tree's source-file mtimes, so all 17 shadowfetch-* .debs and the source tarballs differ in bytes (the two earlier .debs still on disk, -branding and -missions, have identical files, bytes, modes and sizes and differ only in mtimes); they pin every .deb and source file, and acceptance.py record stamps them onto each entry. A rebuilt repository changes both, and every case recorded against these has to be recorded again. Required for publication: SRC-01, PKG-01, UPGRADE-01, DURABLE-01, MISSION-01; the image cases may stay pending. Every case is pending. The case list is carried over from 5.0.0 and every RESULT, waiver and note was dropped rather than copied -- including the six 5.0.0 waivers (MISSION-01, GROK-01, GROK-VISUAL-01, UPGRADE-01, SHADOWCODE-01, STRESS-01), which justified shipping ISO 2d8a72e0 and must be re-argued for 5.0.1 if they are needed at all. ShadowCode is the signed upstream 1.0.1 (7cfed12).
